vectors.description: Request proof whose protected header states the §7.8 digest of the credential object its call presents, as the generator writes it with no input but the arguments the call sends
vectors.reason: The holder names the credential it presents, in the form it is sent, so the proof is bound to that delegation

vectors.description: Request proof that states the digest of the compact VC-JWT its call presents
vectors.reason: A credential sent as a VC-JWT is named by the digest of that form

vectors.description: The proof that names a credential object, beside a copy of it that differs in nothing its issuer signed: other proof metadata, and its signature padded
vectors.reason: A credential is digested by what its issuer signed and the signature bytes, so a copy that differs in nothing signed is the credential named

vectors.description: The proof that names one delegation of the agent, beside another delegation the same user gave the same agent
vectors.reason: A party on the path that holds another delegation of the agent cannot put it in place of the one the holder named: the digests differ

vectors.description: The proof that names a credential, beside one its issuer issued again under the same id with wider scopes
vectors.reason: The statement is a digest of what the issuer signed, not an id, so a credential issued again under the same id is another credential

vectors.description: The proof that names a credential object, beside the same delegation sent as a compact VC-JWT
vectors.reason: A proof names the credential in the form it is sent; the object and the VC-JWT of one delegation have different signed forms, so different digests

vectors.description: Request proof that states "none", for a call that presents no delegation
vectors.reason: A holder that presents no delegation says so, and the statement holds beside none

vectors.description: The proof that states "none", beside a delegation, held by a verifier that requires a proof to name the credential presented
vectors.reason: A delegation added beside a proof that says its call presents none is not the holder's choice

vectors.description: Request proof whose protected header states nothing of its delegation, beside a delegation, held by a verifier that requires a proof to name the credential presented
vectors.reason: A proof that names no delegation is good beside any delegation of its subject, so a verifier that requires naming refuses it

vectors.description: The proof that states nothing of its delegation, for a call that presents none, held by a verifier that requires a proof to name the credential presented
vectors.reason: A holder that presents no delegation states "none"; a proof that states nothing does not say which authority its call is made under

vectors.description: Request proof that states the digest of the credential presented with its hex digits in upper case
vectors.reason: The statement is a credential digest as §7.8 writes one, sha256: and 64 lowercase hex digits, or "none"; any other value is malformed and refused

vectors.description: Request proof that states an array holding the digest of the credential presented
vectors.reason: A statement that is not a string is neither a credential digest nor "none", so it is malformed and refused

vectors.description: The proof that names one delegation, its protected header rewritten after signing to state another, beside that other delegation
vectors.reason: The protected header is part of the JWS signing input, so a statement changed without the holder's key breaks the signature

vectors.description: The proof that names one delegation, its protected header rewritten after signing to state nothing, beside another delegation
vectors.reason: A named proof cannot be made an unnamed one: removing the statement breaks the signature, whether or not the verifier requires naming

vectors.description: Request proof signed over a protected header that holds the parameter twice, the first stating the credential presented and the last another
vectors.reason: Of header parameters that share a name a verifier reads the last or refuses the JWS (RFC 7515 §4), so the first never binds the proof

vectors.description: Request proof whose protected header states the credential presented and whose signed delegationRef names another
vectors.reason: A proof is held to every name of a delegation its signature covers, so one that also names another credential in its payload is refused
